An effect: a braam is one huge processed brass hit, and the sound plays it once, without looping, through a filter that takes seconds to open. Inception’s braams are hits rather than a line; there is no part to write.

An effect: the patch turns one held note into random sample-and-hold blips, the computer “thinking” in 1970s science fiction. The Close Encounters transcription on Songsterr has no tuning, so its notes can’t be read as pitches, and the five-tone motif is a different sound from this one.
A playing style: a gliding lead with vibrato brought in under the wheel. It names no work, and the line is the lesson’s own.
